cases.input: Compare build, buy, and partner options across cost, speed, control, vendor risk, and maintenance effort. Recommend one option and show tradeoffs.
Show an operational snapshot with uptime, latency, error rate, active incident count, alert severity, and a recommended mitigation action.
Map the product organization hierarchy: VP owns platform, growth, and support. Each group has team leads, responsibility areas, and escalation ownership.
Churn increased because onboarding is slow, activation emails are inconsistent, and support handoffs lose context. Connect causes, symptoms, impact, and mitigations.
A support workflow crosses customer, support, engineering, and operations lanes. Customer reports, support triages, engineering fixes, operations deploys, and support closes the loop.
The rollout plan has phases in Q1, Q2, Q3, and Q4: discovery, pilot, controlled rollout, and full adoption. Each phase has milestones, gates, and risks.
The platform is a layered architecture: channels call the API layer, API routes to services, services read and write the data layer, and observability monitors each layer.
A reliability loop observes incidents, prioritizes fixes, deploys mitigations, measures health, and feeds lessons back into planning using feedback paths.
Explain the central concept of product-led growth with clusters for activation, collaboration, monetization, retention, and evidence. Show related principles around the central idea.
Prioritize experiments by impact and effort. Rank onboarding preset, invite nudges, pricing page rewrite, and admin approval changes. Use a two-axis view without creating a new diagram family.

The review contains mixed signals: stronger search intent, weak onboarding confidence, unclear admin ownership, two risks, one recommendation, and three pieces of evidence. The items are related but not sequential.
